round2.evidence: The libc allow-list skip is anchored `^[[:space:]]*@preconcurrency ...import` in k07.sh:75, checks/weaken-check.sh:45 and the hatch-delta awk at swift-quality.md:135. vapor/console-kit writes the chain as `@unsafe @preconcurrency [public] import Glibc|Musl|Android` (21 lines in 7 files, tools 6.2 with strictMemorySafety, which SW-SEC-11 recommends). `bash k07.sh` in a console-kit copy exits 1 and prints all 21 lines. Plant on a branch: `@unsafe @preconcurrency import Glibc` makes weaken-check.sh exit 1 and the hatch-delta awk print it, while plain `@preconcurrency import Glibc` is skipped. concurrency.md:173 S2 (prefix accepted via `sub(/.*@preconcurrency/...)`) is empty on the same tree, so the checks disagree.
round2.fix: Allow leading attributes in all three skips: `^[+]?[[:space:]]*(@[A-Za-z_]+[[:space:]]+)*@preconcurrency...`. Add the `@unsafe` form to the right-hand example in language.md and run all four checks over it.

round2.evidence: The MUST row's e-greps first command (`-e ': RandomNumberGenerator'`, empty output = pass) matches a generic constraint that takes a generator. swift-numerics Sources/_TestSupport/RealTestSupport.swift:30 `static func random<G: RandomNumberGenerator>(using g: inout G)` prints. That is the `using: &g` shape the row itself prescribes, not a custom generator. Other hits on the three trees: none.
round2.fix: Narrow the pattern to conformers: `(struct|class|enum|actor|extension)[^{]*:[^{]*RandomNumberGenerator`. Keep the libc names as they are and add a generic-parameter twin to the watched-green set.

round2.evidence: The G4 cells grep every file with `@main` under Sources, not the executable-target list that the G0 block builds from dump-package. pointfreeco/swift-case-paths has no executable target (G0 prints 'no executable target, SW-CLI does not apply'), yet G4-08, G4-23 and G4-25 each print Sources/CasePathsMacros/Plugin.swift (`@main struct CasePathsPlugin: CompilerPlugin`, a macro plugin that never touches argv or stdout). console-kit prints the example executable Sources/ConsoleLoggerExample/entrypoint.swift while the G1 block skips `*Example` dirs. The rows say they bind every `@main` executable.
round2.fix: Run the G4 greps over the same DIRS array as G1, behind the same G0 guard, or exclude `CompilerPlugin` conformers. Say in the index that a macro plugin is not a CLI.

round2.evidence: P10 runs `grep -rn --include='Package.swift' ... -e '.package(path:' -e 'branch:' -e 'revision:' .` over the whole tree. console-kit prints ./Benchmarks/Package.swift:10 `.package(path: "../")`, a nested Benchmarks fixture manifest that is no product. P10 also reads `branch:` inside comments.

round2.evidence: Step 2 declares `.claude` and `.agents` 'not dirt' and the skill requires the rule set installed in `.claude/`. SwiftPM's SBOM counts untracked files. Plant (tagged v1.0.0, clean tree): SBOM version `v1.0.0`. After `mkdir .claude; echo x > .claude/note` (git status `?? .claude/`): `cyclonedx1-1.7-tool-v1.0.0-modified-all-...json`. Step 8's `grep -L -F -e " : \"$TAG\""` then lists it as a finding. With `.claude/` in .git/info/exclude the SBOM is `v1.0.0` again. A literal run reaches step 8 with a state that step 2 called clean and step 8 cannot pass. My console-kit run printed `v1.2.3-modified` the same way.
round2.fix: Add a step 2 line `printf '.claude/\n.agents/\n' >> .git/info/exclude` (or build from a clean `git worktree`), and state that the exclusion is what makes the SBOM tag exact.

round2.evidence: The pin-grep (swift-quality.md:131) and the U1 inventory only match `swift:[0-9]`, `matrix.swift` and a `swift:` key. round2.evidence: Step 3's second line `diagnose-api-breaking-changes "$LAST" 2>&1 | grep -e 'breaking change' -e 'get revision'` is said to tell apart the two exit-1 causes. On a clean library (console-kit rel-ck vs v1.0.0, exit 0) it prints `No breaking changes detected in ConsoleKit` and `...in ConsoleLogger`, because 'breaking change' is a substring of the pass message. A literal reader sees a hit on a pass, and the pipeline's own exit is grep's. It also runs the whole baseline diagnosis twice. `--scratch-path` placed after the subcommand exits 64 (`Unknown option`), so a scratch-path variant of the line needs it before the subcommand.
round2.fix: Run once into a log, then `grep -e '[1-9][0-9]* breaking change' -e 'get revision' "$LOG"` only when the exit is non-zero. Show `swift package --scratch-path DIR diagnose-api-breaking-changes TAG` if a scratch path is wanted.
